UPSTREAM: sb/intel/bd82x6x: Fix default IRQ mapping The default mapping was probably copy-pasted from a random board and disabled some interrupts (by implicitly clearing some register bits). We provide a new default mapping with some reasoning, that tries to be most compatible (i.e. avoids to use PIRQ E-H that are not shareable on some boards). The following functions had their interrupt pin disabled before: o SATA 2 (explicitly, no board seems to enable the device) o PCIe Root Port #4, #6-#8 (probably by accident) PIRQs used before this change: A-D, F and H. After this change: A-D. UPSTREAM: soc/intel/cannonlake: SoC specific microcode update check For CFL and WHL, Microcode is being loaded from FIT. Both supports the PRMRR/SGX feature. If This is supported the FIT microcode load will set the msr (0x08b) with the Patch id one less than the id in the microcode binary. This results in Microcode getting reloaded again in bootblock and ramstage. Avoid the microcode reload by checking for PRMRR support. CFL and WHL CPU die are based on KBL CPU so we need to have this check, where CNL CPU die is not based on KBL CPU so skip this check for CNL. UPSTREAM: rockchip/rk3399: Fix BL31 bootmem regions The BL31 on RK3399 is split into multiple segments... the majority goes into DRAM, but small parts must be put into SRAM and PMUSRAM. With CB:31123 only the DRAM part was added to memlayout, so the SRAM parts will not be correctly marked in bootmem and BL31 loading fails the selfload check. This patch adds the remaining regions to fix the problem. UPSTREAM: symbols.h: Add macro to define memlayout region symbols When <symbols.h> was first introduced, it only declared a handful of regions and we didn't expect that too many architectures and platforms would need to add their own later. However, our amount of platforms has greatly expanded since, and with them the need for more special memory regions. The amount of code duplication is starting to get unsightly, and platforms keep defining their own <soc/symbols.h> files that need this as well. This patch adds another macro to cut down the definition boilerplate. Unfortunately, macros cannot define other macros when they're called, so referring to region sizes as _name_size doesn't work anymore. This patch replaces the scheme with REGION_SIZE(name). Not touching the regions in the x86-specific <arch/symbols.h> yet since they don't follow the standard _region/_eregion naming scheme. They can be converted later if desired. UPSTREAM: vendorcode/siemens: Cache currently opened hwi file name On every call of hwilib_find_blocks() the CBFS file will be mapped and the contents are parsed to get the offsets for every single block. This is not needed if the CBFS file name is the same for the different calls. This patch adds a storage for the currently opened CBFS file name in CAR_GLOBAL and checks on each call if the file to open is already open. If yes, the file will not be mapped again which saves execution time. Test=Booted mc_tcu3, mc_bdx1 and mc_apl1 and verified that hwinfo.hex is only mapped once across several following hwilib_find_blocks() calls. In addition a test was done to ensure that files with different names get mapped correctly. BACKPORT: FROMGIT: LSM: generalize flag passing to security_capable This patch provides a general mechanism for passing flags to the security_capable LSM hook. It replaces the specific 'audit' flag that is used to tell security_capable whether it should log an audit message for the given capability check. The reason for generalizing this flag passing is so we can add an additional flag that signifies whether security_capable is being called by a setid syscall (which is needed by the proposed SafeSetID LSM). Reason for BACKPORT label: aa_capable() function in security/apparmor/capability.c had slightly different logical operator in 4.14. vs latest upstream code. There is no logical difference between the two. Also, change code in security/chromiumos/lsm.c to take advantage of opts arg in security_capable. This allows to refrain from checking the current syscall number when seeing if security_capable is being called from a setid syscall in the chromiumos LSM. motion_sense: send ODR events to the AP This commits enables the EC to send a motion sense event to the AP when a sensor's ODR is changed. This is done in a way that is backwards compatible on the AP side, in order to enable previous kernels to continue to work (albeit at a loss of new functionality) with up-to-date ECs. Since clients are not required to use a FLUSH when changing ODR, it is possible for the sensor ring to get in a state where it is spreading based on out-of-date delay information, which we observed leading to spreading of overly large intervals, and thus too far into the future. This patch ameliorates that by causing an ODR change to implicitly flush the batching history. FROMGIT: ASoC: da7219: Update TDM usage to be more flexible The previous implementatation was restrictive with regards to BCLK rates for slave mode where the driver would not allow rates the codec couldn't provide itself as clock master. The codec is able to automatically determine and handle whatever rate is provided so this restriction isn't necessary for slave mode. The code was also flawed with regards to setting of the frame offset as using rx_mask to explicitly set the offset has the knock on effect of impacting the min and max channels for the codec, in soc_pcm_hw_params() through the call to soc_pcm_codec_params_fixup(). sepolicy: add type_transistion when chromeos_domain creating under /var Use type_transistion to make sure creating directory "lib" under any directory labelled as cros_var are automatically labelled as cros_var_lib, and vice-versa for "cache", "log", etc. Directories under /var/ like /var/lib, /var/spool, may be deleted and re-created during running of the system, including tests. Previously, we have `restorecon -R -D /var` to fixing SELinux file labels under /var upon boot. But `-D` options makes it only tries to fix when the policy has changed, for example, policy upgrades along with OTA. Recreated /var/lib won't be "fixed" upon any reboot unless the policy has changed. The major reason for not to attempt relabelling everytime is recursive relabelling takes time, and this will slow down Chrome OS boot process. Also, relabelling shouldn't be necessary unless the policy has changed if everything is functioning well. moblab-generic-vm-paladin provision_AutoUpdate has encourterd the situation that after AutoUpdate, files under /var/lib including /var/lib itself is not correctly labeled, because there's no policy upgrade. restorecon simply skips everything to not to slow down boot process with a recursive relabelling, which does nothing most of the time. crrev.com/c/1450654 provides an emergency workaround "fix" like `restorecon -R -D /var/*` which expands to `retorecon -R -D /var/lib /var/cache /var/log ...`, since the last policy is stored at the xattr of the specified directory inode, recreated /var/lib will be treated as relabeling needed since no last policy hash is stored at /var/lib, but only at /var. type_transistion will be the long term fix to let kernel correctly recreate the directory with correct label, and leaving `restorecon -R -D /var` for policy upgrades, or first policy introduction purpose only. CHROMIUM: Fix Bluetooth controller event mask config during system suspend As part of CL:1383763, a few Bluetooth controller events were disabled on suspension, to prevent the system from waking up spuriously. This change is applying the same event mask change as in CL:1383763, but instead of overriding the entire set of events mask it selectively masks out or restores the required events during suspend and resume. In addition, the new Set Event Mask operation introduced in this change is using the BlueZ/NewBlue new suspend and resume infrastucture. As part of suspend/resume operations, BlueZ sends a new MGMT command to the kernel to mask out/restore BT specified events. The kernel adds new functions to handle the Set Event Mask request. The request contains a value and mask parameters to enable overriding only selected events. For more details on the Bluetooth/NewBlue suspend infra refer to CL:1454328 BUG=chromium:930973 TEST=suspend and resume of system and verify event mask is set properly by the kernel. Verify event mask HCI and MGMT messages in BTMON. debugd: Have log_tool read file logs directly log_tool aggregates logs from many different sources. The logs are specified as the output of running a shell command. However, often this shell command is just running cat on some file. There is no need to start another process just to read a file from disk. This change adds two different log types to log_tool: file logs, and command logs. Command logs are the same as before; the output of a shell command. File logs instead just specify a path, and that path is read directly from C++. The process effective uid and effective gid are set before the reads so that file permissions are respected. Additionally, this change splits a couple of log entries that were the combined output of two files into two different log entries. Performance testing over 5 trials showed a .6 second improvement in response time for log_tool when calling GetAllLogs. npcx: pwm: Turn off pwm signal by setting DCRn greater than CTRn. In npcx pwm modules, there're two ways to turn off pwm signal. One is clearing PWR bit in PWMCTL. The other is setting DCRn's value greater than CTRn's. The current pwm driver adopts the first method. But we saw pwm signal doesn't be turned off by the following sequence: 1. pwm_set_raw_duty(ch, 0); 2. pwm_enable(ch, 1); Please notice setting zero in DCRn doesn't mean duty cycle is zero. (NPCX duty cycle: ( (DCRn+1) / (CTRn+1) ) x 100). Hence in step 2, we can observe a very low duty cycle once the driver enabled pwm module. This CL adopts the second method to turn off pwm module. In order to make sure DCRn can be greater than CTRn, we also defined the PWN maximum duty cycle is (0xFFFF -1) since both DCR and CTR are 16-bits registers. CHROMIUM: Fix Bluetooth controller event mask config during system suspend As part of CL:1383763, a few Bluetooth controller events were disabled on suspension, to prevent the system from waking up spuriously. This change is applying the same event mask change as in CL:1383763, but instead of overriding the entire set of events mask it selectively masks out or restores the required events during suspend and resume. In addition, the new Set Event Mask operation introduced in this change is using the BlueZ/NewBlue new suspend and resume infrastucture. As part of suspend/resume operations, BlueZ sends a new MGMT command to the kernel to mask out/restore BT specified events. The kernel adds new functions to handle the Set Event Mask request. The request contains a value and mask parameters to enable overriding only selected events.
